coverage.category: 1. Household employers (domestic workers, carers, nannies)
coverage.found: Labour Law 14/2025 did not regulate domestic work. A separate draft domestic-labour law (reported as 55 articles: licensing of placement offices, contracts, wages, hours) is described as still pending. The President directed the government to finish it in March 2025. No registration duty on households found. Sources: https://www.cnbcarabia.com/137479/2025/03/05/السيسي-يوقع-قانون-العمل-الجديد-ويوجه-بتنظيم-العمالة-المنزلية ; https://www.parlmany.com/News/2/465704/العمالة-المنزلية-تهميش-قانونى-وحقوق-مهدرة-تساؤلات-عن-سبب-استثنائهم . Logged as an unverified watch item.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Scrap collection, transport and recycling fall under Waste Law 202/2020 and the Waste Management Regulatory Authority (WMRA) licensing of non-hazardous waste. About 2,300 licences issued by Mar 2026. Operations must be linked to an electronic system. Micro-enterprises were exempted from licence fees. Scrap import rules were suspended or revised in 2025 (Customs Circular 21/2025, PM decree 288/2025). Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Nothing registry-based. Searched Arabic for scrap/used-goods (روبابيكيا) dealers. Egypt has no dedicated second-hand dealer or pawnbroker register in the sources found. The trade is mostly informal street collectors (carts, tuk-tuks), with a shift to online resale. Fixed shops fall under the general public-shops licensing Law 154/2019 (penalty EGP 20,000-50,000 for operating unlicensed). I found no police purchase-register duty like Oman's weekly buyer list. Pawnbroking is not visible as a licensed activity. No candidate.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Assay and Weights Authority (مصلحة الدمغة والموازين) is modernising: laser stamping, QR/coding plan, central labs re-accredited June 2026, 'Wirshti' workshop financing. No confirmed mandatory dealer register or e-reporting that software could serve. Generic accounting software for gold shops exists (Qoyod). Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Only the state vehicle scrapping/replacement initiative (Form 105 at traffic unit; scrapping yards; a contractor won the MoF tender). No licensing regime for dismantlers or used-parts dealers found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets, animal transport
coverage.found: Veterinary-unit livestock ID ('national number' per animal) plus 1.5%/yr livestock insurance announced 2025, apparently voluntary and in person at veterinary units. No evidence of market-trader or transport permit workflows. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: NFSA (Law 1/2017, PM decree 412/2019) runs mandatory food-establishment registration and inspections, with weekly stats (hundreds of public food premises registered). No butcher- or abattoir-specific recurring filing found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing Egyptian found in the search (only Saudi, Palestinian and Algerian results).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: The General Organisation for Veterinary Services (GOVS, Ministry of Agriculture) licenses outlets selling veterinary medicines; the licence is personal, and clinics also need syndicate registration. Inspection campaigns are reported. No evidence of dispensing registers or e-reporting. Unverified low candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Resources and Irrigation Law 147/2021: art. 70 bans drilling without a licence and bans contracting a driller without a licence; high committee reviews applications; licence 5 years; fee capped at EGP 1,000/yr; art. 107 penalties raised. Sources: https://www.youm7.com/6081041 ; https://almalnews.com/969077/5-بدلًا-من-10-آلاف-جنيه-البرلمان/ . Low-frequency (5-year) workflow. Unverified low candidate.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Could not confirm whether septic-tank vacuum trucks fall under WMRA Law 202/2020 or the water/sanitation holding company. Construction-and-demolition waste transport must be tracked through central rooms (quarterly reports). Folded into the waste candidate; nothing septic-specific.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: One search returned only UAE, Israel and Uzbekistan results. No Egyptian rule found. Not confirmed either way.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Village and town drinking water is run by the state water companies (HCWW and its subsidiaries) with Ministry of Health sampling (about 220k samples, Aug 2026). That leaves no small private operator base to sell compliance software to. Bottled and mineral water plants are Ministry of Health licensed. Only an old 2013 list of 18 licensed brands was found, plus a Sept 2026 raid on an unlicensed plant that counterfeited brands. No periodic reporting duty or testing schedule could be confirmed. NGO village water plants have only old (2013) licensing-difficulty evidence. One low-confidence candidate logged (bottled/filling plants).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Search returned only Syrian, UAE and Palestinian rules. No Egyptian dealer register or e-reporting found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Law 14/2025 arts. 40-43: licences are 1 year and renewable, with EGP 1m deposit and 15-day top-up, a 1% fee cap in year one, and a ministerial decision on records and inspection. Ministerial Decree 272/2025 covers traditional and online agencies. Ministry suspends or closes agencies. A unified employment platform is being built. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Burial permit and death certificate come from the health office (free). Cemetery plots are sold or allotted by governorates and the Housing Ministry; brokers reported selling non-burial land. No licensing or recurring filing for private burial services found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies (associations, charities, halal/kosher)
coverage.found: NGO Law 149/2019 and its regulations (PM decree 104/2021): ministry e-platform, 36 e-services, books and accounts on prescribed templates, budget review. Halal/kosher supervision not searched. NGO candidate logged.

coverage.category: 18. Informal transport (minibus, taxi, moto-taxi)
coverage.found: New Traffic Law: tuk-tuks licensed as motorcycle taxis; governors cap numbers and set tariffs; a 20-year age limit for mass-transit vehicles is announced but no start date found. No operator-side recurring filing found. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: CBE exchange-company licensing rules (one unofficial source cites EGP 25m capital) mean few, large regulated firms. Street vendors and market traders not searched.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises (tattoo, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, food producers, hunting)
coverage.found: Nurseries: Ministry of Social Solidarity licences via directorates; July 2025 six-month temporary licence for regularisation with capacity cap and child-protection policy; candidate logged. Driving schools: nothing Egyptian found. Food producers: NFSA (see 7). Tattoo and hunting outfitters not reached.

coverage.category: EG-1. Real-estate brokers (Egypt-specific)
coverage.found: Jan 2026 amendment to the executive regulations of Law 120/1982: mandatory GOEIC register for brokers, electronic records of contracts and commissions, 6-month transition ended about 25 Jul 2026, penalties up to 2 years and EGP 1m. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: EG-2. Private clinics, medical centres and hospitals licensing
coverage.found: Health Ministry e-licensing and coding system launched Feb 2025 (digital licence, QR). About 38,000 clinics, 4,620 centres and 1,460 private hospitals got a 15-day order to display prices and issue tax invoices. A draft law sets 5-year renewal. Weak licensing candidate; the e-receipt part is already in round 1.

coverage.category: EG-3. Non-hazardous waste licence holders (WMRA, Law 202/2020)
coverage.found: See candidate: about 2,300 licences, new per-waste-type licences, packaging compaction category, electronic inbound and sales reporting.

coverage.category: EG-4. Subsidised bread bakeries and ration grocers (Ministry of Supply)
coverage.found: 'Direct deduction' system started 1 Aug 2026 for about 30,000 bakeries: bank-settled flour purchases, flour stock declarations in some governorates (Sharqia), electronic balances that lapse if flour is not bought. Government-run; no private bakery software found. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: EG-5. Livestock and poultry farm operating licences (Law 70/2009) and livestock ID
coverage.found: Ministry of Agriculture issued about 804 operating licences (new and renewals) in the first half of Dec 2025 alone. Biosecurity campaign. Only foreign farm software found. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: EG-6. Quarries and mines (Mineral Resources Law 198/2014, amended 145/2019)
coverage.found: Royalty 5-20% of annual production value set by regulation, plus rent and fees. Periodic production reports not confirmed. State quarry platform and truck management planned. Candidate logged as unverified.

coverage.category: EG-7. Diving and marine-activity centres (Ministry of Tourism)
coverage.found: Tourism Ministry inspects diving and marine centres (22 licensed plus 17 pending; 35 marine-activity centres inspected in one report) and suspends technical directors. Tiny universe. Weak.

coverage.category: EG-8. LPG cylinder depots
coverage.found: About 3,008 distribution centres; Petrogas SCADA is state-side; depot margin is a few pounds per cylinder. No depot licensing or reporting rule found. Weak.

coverage.category: EG-9. Imported mobile phones (NTRA and Customs 'Telefoni' IMEI registry)
coverage.found: Consumer-side duty registry with duties up to 38.5% after a 90-day grace period. No retailer filing duty found. Weak.

coverage.category: EG-10. Private security-guard companies
coverage.found: One search found nothing Egyptian. Unknown.

coverage.category: Pharmacies, drug stores and private pharmaceutical warehouses: controlled and narcotic drug registers
coverage.found: Law 182/1960 (text on lawyeregypt, possibly pre-amendment) sets concrete recurring duties. Art. 18: narcotics register in a numbered, stamped book, entries same day. Art. 17: prescriptions kept. Art. 23: signed six-month statement of received/dispensed/remaining stock, due in the first 15 days of January and July on an official form. Art. 31: ten-year retention. Art. 50: pharmacy inspectors review registers. EDA (which took over from the Ministry) is expanding controlled outlets via the Egyptian Drug Trading Co. (Mar 2025). No electronic narcotics register or named software for it was found. EPTTS track and trace is already rejected in round 1; this is a different workflow. Candidate logged, narrow.

coverage.category: Hotels, tourist establishments and Airbnb-style short-let units (Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Law 1/1973)
coverage.found: Law 1/1973 has been replaced by Law 8/2022 on hotel and tourist establishments. Ministerial Decision 209/2025 (April 2025) created a licensed 'Holiday Home' category (units of 1+ room, suite or villa, in a tourist area or distinguished compound). Owners notify the Ministry electronically on its website form to obtain a tourism operating certificate (شهادة الصلاحية السياحية). Hotels must file guest-data notifications (four-part name, national ID or passport, address, nationality, mobile) through the 'tourism movement linking system' (منظومة ربط مفردات الحركة السياحية), coordinated with the Tourism and Antiquities Police. Hotels need a token device, and entry is manual or by integration. The source is the Hotels Chamber letter of Oct 2022, and the later press item is undated. Whether Holiday Home units must use the same system is unverified. Two candidates logged.

coverage.category: Industrial and commercial shop licensing under the 2019 unified licensing law (Law 152/2020 on micro, small and medium enterprises and Law 143/2024 on commercial and industrial licences) and the GAFI/ITIDA one-stop platform
coverage.found: I could not confirm a 'Law 143/2024' on commercial and industrial licences in any search result, so treat that reference as unverified. What is confirmed: the Public Shops Law 154/2019 and its 2020 regulation. The licence service launched on the Masr Digital platform (Digital Vault) in July 2026, with immediate provisional permits, a 50% fee discount for a limited period, status tracking, binding agency deadlines and electronic payment. Industrial: Law 15/2017 (temporary one-year operating permits, renewable); a bill to regularize unlicensed factories with 3 extra years was in parliament (date unconfirmed). The state portal is free and now covers the filing. Possible residual gap is licence-expiry and multi-document tracking, with no private product found. Candidate logged as weak.

coverage.category: Taxi, ride-hailing, tour bus and goods-transport operators: Transport Ministry and Traffic Department licences, plus Land Transport Regulatory Authority
coverage.found: Goods-transport activity licence and per-vehicle operating card from the Land Transport Regulatory Authority, with fees by gross weight (EGP 500/300/150 per card in the old 2017 draft; the Cabinet later set annual fees for goods-transport licences and renewals, 2022). Periodic technical inspection plus compulsory insurance are needed for the traffic licence. Mobile technological centres (hotline 15558) do licensing and inspection on site. Ride-hailing falls under Law 87/2018 (TNC companies must prove drivers' social insurance). No fleet-compliance expiry tool was found. Existing: Trukto (freight marketplace), Tareeqi (bus tracking), general GPS vendors. I could not verify the current LTRA platform or licence categories. One candidate logged.

coverage.category: Customs clearance and small importers/exporters: Advance Cargo Information, Nafeza and the registry of importers/exporters (Law 121/1982 on commercial register for importers)
coverage.found: New Executive Regulation, Ministerial Decree 271/2026 (about 22 Jul 2026), replaces Decree 846/2017 under Law 121/1982 as amended by Law 4/2026. The regulator GOEIC must build an electronic platform within six months for registration, renewal, re-registration and data amendment. Expanded disclosure and reporting. Goods grouped into 21 commodity groups. Capital payable in convertible foreign currency. Registration lasts 5 years, with renewal windows 90 days either side under the old rules (to re-verify). Factory registration for goods imported into Egypt (Decree 43/2016, amended by 195/2022): documents with expiry dates (quality certificates, trademarks, industrial register) must be renewed within 30 days. A two-week warning is followed by a one-year suspension, then delisting. In July 2026 the importers' division complained of registration delays, asking for a 45-day maximum. Two candidates logged. Round-1 covered ACI/Nafeza, not this importer-side registration.

coverage.category: Fuel stations, car workshops and garages: petroleum and oil-product licensing, and car-repair or washing workshops
coverage.found: EGPC (Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation) runs inspection campaigns on fuel stations, with 2025-26 findings on pump calibration and meter tampering, water in tanks, missing automatic gauging, fire-fighting kit and unlicensed stations or LPG outlets lacking civil-defence conditions. Stations are run by dealers under marketing companies, so the compliance data flows through the marketing company. I found no private compliance software. Workshops: no official licensing guide found; only generic public-shops licensing and civil-defence rules (2025 Cabinet fire-safety regulations). Waste: the WMRA decision on used cooking oil (Aug 2025; Law 202/2020 and registration on the WIMS site) is the clearest new waste licence found; used engine oil handling for workshops was not confirmed. Candidates logged as weak.

candidates.name: Non-hazardous waste licensee compliance and movement-reporting tool (scrap yards, collectors, recyclers, packaging compaction)
candidates.buyer: Owners of scrap yards, waste collectors and haulers, small recycling plants and packaging-compaction sites holding or needing a WMRA licence. About 2,300 licences issued by Mar 2026; many are family firms.
candidates.trigger: Waste Law 202/2020 and executive regulations: activity licences are being split by waste type, with renewals counted from the expiry date. Operators must link inbound waste and sales movements to the authority's electronic system (WMRA board, 28 Mar 2026). Packaging compaction licences run one year, and compaction data feeds a planned extended producer responsibility system.
candidates.evidence: https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8253922 (fetched: 2,300 licences, per-type licences, electronic linkage, 1-year compaction licence, renewal rule) ; https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5585557.aspx (minister asks to extend licence terms) ; https://almalnews.com/1348504/وزيرة-البيئة-إعفاء-الشركات-متناهية-الصغر-العاملة/ (micro firms exempt from fees) ; https://www.youm7.com/6039095 (first phase of digital waste system) ; scrap import rule churn: https://www.iss-shipping.com/advisories/new-regulations-on-scrap-material-inspections-in-egypt/
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: waste-plant / scrap-yard program + weighbridge + WMRA reporting): no Egyptian product found. Only the state WIMS app/portal and generic inventory software (Daftra-type templates, freelancer builds). Unclear whether the state system exposes an API or accepts private-software data.
candidates.unchecked: The exact format and frequency of WMRA movement reporting. Whether scrap dealers (as opposed to recyclers) must hold a licence. Whether there is an API or bulk-upload route. Licence term after the board's review. How many small yards are actually licensed versus informal. Willingness to pay.

candidates.name: Overseas and domestic recruitment agency records, deposit and renewal manager
candidates.buyer: Licensed Egyptian employment companies (joint-stock, LLC, one-person company) placing Egyptians abroad or domestically, and applicants for new licences. The universe is probably hundreds (unverified).
candidates.trigger: Labour Law 14/2025 arts. 40-43: licence 1 year renewable; EGP 1m deposit that must be topped up within 15 days after deductions; worker fee cap 1% of wage in year one; ministerial decision on required records, premises and ad rules (Decree 272/2025 covers traditional and online agencies); the ministry suspends or closes non-compliant agencies (10 stopped in Nov 2025); a unified employment platform is in preparation.
candidates.evidence: https://banker.news/122911 (fetched: conditions, deposit, 1-year licence, 1% cap, art. 42 records) ; https://www.dostor.org/print.aspx?id=5582383 ; https://hapijournal.com/2025/11/05/إيقاف-وإغلاق-نشاط-10-شركات-إلحاق-عمالة-م/ ; https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8206535 (penalty warning) ; https://www.parlmany.com/News/7/592964/القانون-يحدد-شروط-مزاولة-عمليات-إلحاق-المصريين-للعمل-بالداخل-أو
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: recruitment-office management program + contracts + Egypt): none found. Only generic contract tools (Daftra) and state e-systems for contract approval and Libya linkage. The ministry's unified platform could crowd out a private tool.
candidates.unchecked: The ministerial decision's list of mandatory records and reporting. Number of licensed agencies. Whether the unified platform replaces private record-keeping. Price tolerance. Which sub-segment (overseas, Gulf, domestic) is biggest.

candidates.name: Real-estate broker register compliance kit (GOEIC registration, contract and commission e-records, renewals)
candidates.buyer: Individual brokers and small brokerage offices; also chambers of commerce, which host GOEIC desks (for example the Kafr El-Sheikh chamber). The universe is large but informal (no count found; about 1,000 trained so far).
candidates.trigger: Law 120/1982 executive regulations amended 25 Jan 2026: mandatory register run by the General Authority for Export and Import Control, with electronic records of contracts and commissions, training and tax compliance. The 6-month transition ended about 25 Jul 2026. Unlicensed practice carries jail and fines from EGP 50k up to EGP 1m. Enforcement arrests in Apr 2026.
candidates.evidence: https://hapijournal.com/2026/04/26/وزارة-الاستثمار-استحداث-ضوابط-جديدة-ل/ (fetched) ; https://www.egypttelegraph.com/article/239068/الغرامة-تصل-مليون-جنيه-تعرف-على-عقوبة (fetched: commercial register and tax card, penalties) ; https://www.alborsaanews.com/2026/01/20/1943741 ; https://www.dostor.org/5651767 ; https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5604653.aspx (blocked, 403, snippet only)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: brokerage office program + GOEIC register): only general real-estate CRMs (Zoho EstateCRM, iMaxCRM and similar at about $50 per user). No Egypt-specific compliance or register tool seen.
candidates.unchecked: Whether GOEIC's electronic record has a defined format or portal that software could feed. Real number of brokers. Whether most brokers will pay at all. Required renewal frequency and fees. Risk that the authority publishes its own free tool.

candidates.name: Nursery (daycare) licence, capacity and staff-file manager
candidates.buyer: Private nurseries in Egypt (count not confirmed), especially those in the regularisation drive.
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Social Solidarity: six-month temporary licence (Jul 2025) conditional on staff files, qualified staff or training, a child-protection policy, capacity stated in the licence, and ground- or first-floor premises. Licensing by directorate; Jan 2026 minister promised easier licensing.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: nursery management program + ministry licence): Jam3ati (Arabic SaaS script), OpenEduCat page for Egypt, old Mostaql/Khamsat custom programs. None ties to ministry licence evidence.
candidates.unchecked: Number of nurseries; whether staff-file inspections are routine and recurring; renewal term; any compulsory records or reports beyond the initial licence.

candidates.name: NGO (Law 149/2019) books, budget and annual-report pack
candidates.buyer: Small associations and foundations (tens of thousands registered; 26,500 sought regularisation by the deadline), regional unions, donors that sponsor grantees.
candidates.trigger: Law 149/2019 and regulations (PM decree 104/2021): accounts in books set by prescribed templates, budget review, e-platform with 36 services.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: NGO management program + ministry reports): no specific product found; ministry platform handles registration, not accounting.
candidates.unchecked: Current annual filing requirements and deadlines; whether the ministry accepts any software output; donor money that might pay; very low spend per association.

candidates.name: Subsidised-bread bakery flour and direct-deduction reconciliation
candidates.category: EG-4 Subsidised bakeries and ration grocers
candidates.buyer: About 30,000 subsidised bakeries and their owners (Bakeries Division).
candidates.trigger: 'Direct deduction' system began 1 Aug 2026 (Ministerial directive 14/2026): flour bought through bank settlement, daily bread output tied to flour, electronic balances that lapse if flour is not bought, stock declarations required in some governorates (Sharqia), penalties priced at EGP 2,966 per sack of unmatched flour.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: bakery management program + direct deduction): none found. Government-run system; bakers use Ministry POS and bank accounts.
candidates.unchecked: Whether bakers keep their own flour and bread books; whether government systems already show balance and reconciliation; the cash-subsidy switch may change the system; unlikely to be a paying, software-minded buyer.

candidates.category: EG-5 Livestock and poultry farm licences
candidates.buyer: Poultry, cattle, feed and fish-farm operators needing renewal (Ministry of Agriculture livestock sector).
candidates.trigger: Law 70/2009 on poultry farms and ministerial decisions: about 804 operating licences (new and renewals) in half a month of Dec 2025; biosecurity campaign.
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: poultry farm management program + operating licence): only NavFarm (India) and generic farm software. No licence-aware Egyptian product found.
candidates.unchecked: Actual renewal period and required periodic records (vaccination, mortality, movement); the 2025 volume figure may be a campaign burst. Large integrators dominate poultry.

candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic: quarry/crusher management program + royalty): no Egyptian product; foreign weighbridge/quarry suites exist (Proginov, OpenWeigh, Quarry360).
candidates.unchecked: Whether operators file periodic production returns and in what form; royalty percentages (sources conflict); who the real small-operator buyer is.

verified.name: Non-hazardous waste licensee compliance and movement-reporting tool (scrap yards, collectors, recyclers, packaging compaction)
verified.reason:
The licence duty is real and in force. Article 29 of Egypt's Waste Management Law 202/2020 bans non-hazardous waste collection, transport and treatment without a WMRA licence. The executive regulations set the licence term and renewal. Breaching Articles 29 or 30 carries a fine of EGP 100,000 to 1,000,000, and a repeat offence carries prison. About 2,300 licences had been issued by March 2026 (El Watan, 28 Mar 2026).

The core job of filing licences and reporting movements to the authority is done by the free state system. The national waste information system (WIMS) is run by WMRA and was built with GIZ under the national solid waste programme. As of August 2026 the minister described it as issuing licences, approvals and permits electronically. It also hosts the EPR packaging registration, which the authority describes as ready to launch. So the "electronic linkage" the claim relies on is the government's own portal, not a gap for a private tool.

Several points I could not confirm:
- The linking of inbound waste and sales to the electronic system appears only as a proposal in the March 2026 board article.
- No reporting frequency or format is published.
- I found no API or bulk-upload route, so a private tool could only re-enter data into WIMS.
- I could not confirm that scrap dealers, as opposed to recyclers and collectors, must hold a licence.

What would be left is a generic yard and weighbridge ERP, which Odoo, Daftra and local developers already cover. The buyers are informal family firms with low willingness to pay, and micro firms are exempt from fees.

Suggested score 3 of 10: the penalty is real, but nothing proves a recurring reporting duty that a private product could own. The free state portal is the filing channel, with no integration route found, and the remaining value is commodity inventory software sold to a hard-to-reach informal market.

verified.name: Overseas and domestic recruitment agency records, deposit and renewal manager
verified.reason:
DUTY (real and in force): Egypt's Labour Law 14/2025 was published in the Official Gazette, issue 18, on 3 May 2025. Art. 40 says only licensed private employment agencies may place workers, and they must be a joint-stock company, partnership limited by shares, LLC or one-person company. Art. 41 sets the licence terms: 1 year and renewable, fee of at most EGP 10k, minimum capital of EGP 250k for domestic-only work or EGP 500k for work abroad, and a deposit or bank guarantee of at least EGP 1m that must be restored within 15 days of notice after any deduction. Art. 42 leaves the required records, premises rules, inspection and advertising rules to a ministerial decision. Art. 43 caps what an agency may charge a worker at 1% of first-year wages. Ministerial Decree 272/2025 regulates both domestic and overseas placement, and the ministry gave existing firms a grace period to comply. Penalties reported in the press are imprisonment and/or a fine of EGP 20k-100k for operating without a licence or breaking the implementing decrees. Closure is mandatory for unlicensed operation. The ministry suspended or closed 10 companies in Nov 2025, and police raided 26 unlicensed firms in Gharbia and Menoufia in Aug 2026. I could not find the decree's actual list of required records or any periodic reporting duty, which is what the product would depend on. The duties I could confirm are an annual renewal and a deposit top-up only after a deduction. Neither is a frequent recurring workflow.

COMPETITION (partly contradicts 'none found'): Daftra, an Arabic cloud ERP that sells in Egypt and supports Egyptian e-invoicing, has a dedicated recruitment-office module. It covers worker files and pricing, request tracking with contract dates and terms, foreign partner-office files and payments, invoicing, CRM and automatic accounting. Qoyod advertises a similar recruitment program. Both are built mainly for agencies bringing workers into the Gulf, and neither shows Egypt-specific features such as tracking the deposit, the 1% cap or the decree's record list. The ministry already runs e-systems to approve overseas contracts and offers e-services for workers. An industry federation (reported on youm7) has proposed a unified digital licensing system linking agencies to the ministry, holding each company's capital, guarantee letter and complaints record. If that is built, it would cover the deposit and licence tracking.

MARKET: The ministry official in charge of these agencies cited 1,050 licensed placement companies and about 500k workers going abroad a year (youm7, Aug 2023). No current count is published, and the ministry says it is still building a public database.

WHY UNVERIFIABLE AND NOT CONFIRMED: The duty is real, but the record-keeping obligations that would justify recurring software are not public in the decree text I could find. General recruitment-agency ERPs already exist in Arabic. Whether the state platform will take over the core job is unknown.

SCORE 3: The pain is real and the penalties are severe, but the compliance events I could confirm (yearly renewal, deposit top-ups only after a deduction) happen too rarely to sell a subscription on their own. Existing Arabic recruitment ERPs and a likely ministry platform squeeze any space for a niche tool. About 1,000 agencies, many of them informal and cash-based, is a small market with uncertain willingness to pay.

verified.name: Real-estate broker register compliance kit (GOEIC registration, contract and commission e-records, renewals)
verified.reason: The duty is real and in force in Egypt. Law 120/1982 on commercial agency, as amended by Law 21/2022 to cover real-estate brokerage, has executive regulations amended by a ministerial decision of 25 Jan 2026. GOEIC (the General Authority for Export and Import Control, under the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade) must keep an official broker register with registration and renewal conditions. Brokers must keep electronic records of transactions, contracts and commissions, complete training, have a commercial register and tax card, and meet disclosure rules. The 6-month deadline to register passed on 25 Jul 2026. Breaches can lead to suspension or removal from the register. The reported penalty for unregistered practice is jail and/or a fine of EGP 50k to over EGP 1m, and the authorities arrested an unlicensed broker in Apr 2026. Some secondary sites cite a 'Law 578 of 2026', which I could not confirm and which looks like a mislabel. I found no Egypt-specific software that keeps the required contract and commission records or handles GOEIC registration. Competitors are only generic CRMs and Saudi accounting tools. However, GOEIC registration is a hybrid process: online training (EGP 1,500) and branch booking (or hotline 19591), then documents and fees in person at a branch. Property Finder Egypt signed a protocol with GOEIC on 9 Jul 2026 to train its partner brokers. That gives a large portal both a distribution channel and a natural position to bundle compliance features, so the 'nothing does the core job' finding is fragile. No register count was found, and the only figure is about 1,000 brokers trained, so the market is unquantified and largely informal. The score is low (3) for four reasons. Registration is a one-off, in-person step that software cannot do for the broker. The recurring duty to keep e-records has no published format, portal or reporting frequency for software to feed. Renewal frequency and fees are unknown. And the buyers are mostly informal sole brokers with low willingness to pay, while Property Finder and similar portals could add the feature for free.

verified.name: Foreign-factory registration document-expiry tracker for Egyptian importers and sourcing agents
verified.reason:
The duty is real, and no dedicated software does this job. Decree 43/2016, amended by Decree 195/2022, requires foreign factories and brand owners exporting listed goods to Egypt to be on GOEIC's register. Documents with an expiry date (such as quality certificates) must be renewed within 30 days of expiry. Firms that miss this get a two-week warning, then a one-year ban from exporting to Egypt, and their goods cannot clear customs (Enterprise, Apr 2022). GOEIC enforced this at scale: 224 firms suspended in Sep 2020, 324 warned in Oct 2020, and hundreds suspended in 2022. I found no repeal or 2025-26 amendment, but I also found no 2025-26 primary source confirming the decree is in force today. Several news pages show 2026 dates in the header while the articles are older (the Parlmany article is from 2017).

Competition: Arabic and English searches turned up only GOEIC itself, law firms, the German-Arab Chamber and customs consultancies. I found no tracker, and no proof either way that GOEIC's portal sends expiry alerts.

Market: I could not find the total number of registered factories. GOEIC publishes additions and removals monthly, but only in batches (for example, 16 entries in one late-2022 batch).

Why the score is low: the legal duty sits on the foreign factory or its authorised agent, not on the Egyptian SME. Documents renew only every one to three years. The buyer pool is small and unquantified, and customs consultants probably include this monitoring in their service at no extra charge. An expiry tracker is technically trivial, so it is easy to copy and hard to charge for.

verified.name: Guest-data notification and check-in tool for small hotels, guesthouses and Holiday Home units (tourism movement linking system)
verified.reason:
The duty is real. Under a circular from the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, enforced from 1 November 2022, hotels must notify guest data (four-part name, national ID or passport number, address, nationality, mobile) through the electronic 'tourism movement linking system' for each stay. Non-compliant hotels face 'legal and administrative measures' based on reports from the Tourism and Antiquities Police (Dostor, 20 Oct 2022). No specific decree number or fine was found.

The claim is refuted because the core job is already done in two ways:
- The state system itself is free and mandatory, and lets token-holding hotels enter guests manually or upload data directly. Small hotels without a PMS are meant to use it.
- Per the Hotels Chamber, quoted by Albawabh News (seen only as a search snippet; the page returned 403), hotels running PMS such as Opera or Comsys are integrated directly with the Interior Ministry's foreigners-security system to avoid entering data twice.

Access goes through Ministry-issued token devices, no third-party API or spec is public, and the Holiday Home decisions (March and November 2025) say nothing about guest notification. A solo founder would be selling a thin wrapper around a free government portal they may not be allowed to connect to. The market is also small: about 234k rooms nationally, concentrated in large hotels; I found no exact count of hotels.

verified.name: Short-term rental (Airbnb host) GCT and registration toolkit
verified.reason:
The duty is not yet in force. The House approved the GCT (Amendment of Schedules) Order, 2026 to take effect on 1 April 2027 (Gleaner, 30 Apr 2026). But EY tax executive John Butler says it is unclear whether the order taxes Airbnb at all, because it changes only the tourism GCT rate (10% to 15%) and no accommodation definitions. No TAJ guidance exists yet on registration, the threshold, or whether Airbnb or the host collects. The JTB registration and licensing bill is still stalled, so neither half of the "registration toolkit" duty can be confirmed today.

Hosts who do register will file the same monthly Form 4A GCT return as any other business. That return must be filed online through TAJ's portal; one third-party site puts the late-filing penalty at J$5,000 a month. Local GCT tools such as YaadBooks already handle that return, so the open gap is only Airbnb payout reconciliation, not filing. The registration threshold is reportedly J$15M a year (about US$95k), unconfirmed, though the claim's own source says J$10M. Either way, most small hosts would likely fall below it, which shrinks the number of paying users.

Market size: AirDNA counts about 5,300 active listings in seven main markets (Gleaner, Apr 2026), well short of a full national count. Many of these are hosts below the threshold. Score 3: the trigger is uncertain and the start is delayed, the likely payers are few, and a free state portal plus local GCT accounting tools already do the core filing. It should be revisited once TAJ publishes guidance before April 2027.

verified.name: Produce dealer and farmer receipt-book compliance (Agricultural Produce Act)
verified.reason:
The duty is real and is being enforced. Under Jamaica's Agricultural Produce Act, as amended by Act No. 19 of 2023 (passed by the Senate on 15 Dec 2023), produce on the road must be accompanied by a receipt, and anyone buying or trading produce must have one. Maximum penalties rose from J$250k or 3 months to J$3M or 3 years. Courts are applying it: on 27 Jul 2026 two men in St Catherine were each fined J$100k, one for not having a receipt and one for not issuing one. In January 2026 the JAS told farmers to register on RADA's ABIS system and buy receipt books from JAS offices.

I found no digital receipt, e-invoice or QR traceability product for produce sales, from the state or from vendors. The 2013 police SMS verification tool has no sign of ever launching. The 2024 RADA app covers registration and extension visits only. Recent QR work covers exports such as castor oil and Blue Mountain coffee, not this. So the claim is confirmed on its own terms.

It still scores low, for four reasons:
1. The legal instrument is a serialized, JAS-issued paper receipt book tied to the farmer's ABIS registration number. Nothing I found allows an app to stand in for it, and I could not read the Act text: the parliament PDF is a scan, FAOLEX returned 403 and the MOA page returned 503. A private app would have to work alongside the paper book rather than replace it.
2. The people who issue receipts are mostly small farmers with low willingness to pay. Buyers such as supermarkets and hotels only need to keep the receipts, which is a light pain.
3. The dealer and traveller licence provisions were never activated as of 2012, and I found no count of current licences. The market is only roughly sized: about 160,000+ registered farmers, with an unknown number of licensed dealers.
4. Distribution would have to go through RADA and JAS, which control the receipt system.

The best wedge is a buyer-side tool for supermarkets, hotels and exporters to capture receipts and keep a traceability log, but how much they would pay for it is unproven.

verified.name: Private security company compliance: PSRA licence expiry, guard roster and statutory payroll
verified.reason: The duty is real and in force. Under Jamaica's PSRA Act, security firms and every guard must be licensed or registered with the PSRA. Firms are covered by a sector-specific Minimum Wage (Industrial Security Guards) Order: J$16,000 per 40-hour week from 1 Jun 2025, rising to J$17,000 from 1 Jul 2026, with firearm premium and life-insurance allowances. Registered firms must also deduct PAYE, NIS and NHT. A client who hires an unregistered guard becomes liable, according to the PSRA. I found no specific fine amounts, the exact licence term, or a passed amendment to the Act. Market: the PIOJ Economic and Social Survey counted 331 security organisations registered or renewed in 2025 (311 in 2024) and 30,013 individual registrants. On competition, I found no single PSRA-aware tool that tracks licence expiry alongside rosters and Jamaican statutory payroll, so the claim holds narrowly. But the parts are all covered already: Jamaican payroll products do the deductions and S01/S02 returns (YaadBooks has a free tier; also HeadOffice, BizPay, iCoPAY, Workzoom, an Odoo JM module, and WallPost via Dawgen); global guard tools do scheduling (TrackTik/Trackforce, TEAM, GuardsPro, free Everhour); and the PSRA has offered online licence renewal for individuals since Nov 2021. Scored 3 because the market is very small (about 330 firms, many of them large and probably on enterprise or custom systems) and the only new piece, licence-expiry tracking, is a thin layer on payroll and scheduling tools that already exist, and a spreadsheet can do it. Willingness to pay among small firms is unproven, though the guard minimum-wage order and its allowances make guard payroll a little harder than ordinary payroll.

verified.reason:
The duty is real and in force. Section 3 of Jamaica's Early Childhood Act 2005 says every ECI must register with the ECC. Section 5 lets an ECI operate on a permit before registration. Sections 22, 24 and 25 provide closure orders and offences, with fines or imprisonment, though I could not confirm the exact fine amounts. Registration needs fire and public health reports and staff medical, police and food-handler records, and the ECC inspects against 12 standards. The Gleaner reported on 22 Aug 2026 that 2,428 ECIs were operating as at March 2026 and that about 4% were non-compliant.

I found no Jamaican or ECC-specific software that does the core job. Registration is still a paper form plus a J$1,500 fee paid at NCB. The only local school platform, My School Jamaica (Comsol), targets primary and secondary schools.

The score stays low for three reasons:
- **Low frequency:** registration is mostly one-off, followed by occasional inspections, and I found no fixed renewal cycle.
- **Weak buyers:** many basic schools are poor, community-run operations under pressure not to charge fees, so willingness to pay is weak.
- **Small market:** about 2,400 institutions.

verified.reason:
The duty is real and in force. The Spirit Licence Act (1928, last amended 2012) is listed as current on the Ministry of Justice laws site. It requires a Parish Court licence to sell spirits. Licences last one year, all expire on 31 March, and the applicant must post a 21-day notice before the court session, get a police recommendation, get a health certificate and pay at the Inland Revenue Department (IRD). I could not open the statute itself (laws.moj.gov.jm returned HTTP 503), so the 31 March date and the penalties come from secondary sources. Those sources are the Observer in 2019 and the Gleaner in 2015, and both say the licence must be renewed every year. The penalty is small: J$5,000 or 6 months, plus J$200 a day for not displaying the licence.

Nothing else does the core job of reminding owners and preparing the application pack. Since 2022 the state lets applicants fill in forms from parishcourt.gov.jm and email them, but the police and health steps are still done in person, and I found no reminder app, software or agent service.

Market: in 2020 the Local Government Minister cited 11,013 community bars, of which only about 30% were properly licensed. Restaurants and liquor retailers are on top of that.

Why the score is low: the penalty is small and rarely enforced, and about 70% of bars ignore the duty. The buyers are very small operators who are hard to reach and unlikely to pay. The work happens once a year, and most of it is in-person steps that software cannot remove. A seasonal reminder plus a printed or WhatsApp checklist is about the most a product can do. The claim's fire-certificate and gaming parts were not confirmed as part of the spirit licence.
